proposal.title: Private IBM Cloud Object Storage with an existing service ID
proposal.body: Scope: one private versioned IBM Cloud Object Storage bucket in an existing COS instance. An existing IAM service ID gets object upload, read and delete access. Anonymous access is blocked and IBM manages the encryption keys. au-syd is a candidate region and has not been verified. There is no compute, no AI and no private endpoint. Account, COS instance and service ID identifiers will be supplied separately as inputs. This is a design only, with no deployment.

data.label: Synthetic document bucket
data.description: A private bucket in an existing COS instance with object versioning on, anonymous and public access blocked, and IBM-managed encryption. It holds synthetic documents only. Candidate region au-syd has not been verified. The COS instance ID is a required input.

requirementDrafts.rationale: If the access scope is too broad, documents could be exposed or deleted by the wrong identity.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "An existing service identity must upload, read and delete objects. Block anonymous access"
requirementDrafts.statement: Only the existing service identity can upload, read and delete objects in the bucket. All anonymous and public access is denied.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Because the identity can delete objects, versioning protects against accidental loss.
requirementDrafts.statement: Object versioning is enabled so that overwritten or deleted documents can be recovered.

requirementDrafts.rationale: The region choice decides where the data lives. The country requirement has not been stated yet.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Use au-syd as a candidate region"
requirementDrafts.statement: The bucket is placed in a region that meets the confirmed data-country requirement. au-syd is only a candidate until this is confirmed.

Do not just recite a checklist or demand that a junior developer repair product internals. response.message: Good news: the local check passed for design revision 2. It ran with no failures or blockers, so the private bucket contract works as expected against an S3-compatible emulator. That emulator isn't IBM COS, though, so IBM IAM, the endpoints and the region are still unchecked, and the biggest open gap is where the data is allowed to live. Which country must these synthetic documents stay in? For example Australia, which would support au-syd, or "no restriction".
